A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RATE study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v4 reports original RATE experiments on memory-intensive environments, Atari, MuJoCo, and Action Associative Retrieval, together with memory-component, curriculum-learning, and MRV ablations.

after.justification: v5 retains original empirical evaluations and reports additional memory-model comparisons, OracleDT controls, and noise and hyperparameter ablations.

M1.justification: The proposed RATE procedure retains segmented trajectory processing, recurrent memory embeddings, cached hidden states, and cross-attention MRV updates. Algorithms 1–2 primarily reformulate the existing method. Appendix D newly discloses disabling RATE's decoder feed-forward block, but does not establish that this implementation differed in v4; this is documentation rather than a demonstrated method revision.

E1.justification: All benchmark families, including AAR, are retained. Memory Maze training data change from the supplied random-object-navigation trajectories described in v4 Appendix C to Dreamer-generated trajectories in v5 Appendix B. Minigrid evaluation extends from the roughly 60-cell range plotted in v4 Figure 5(d) to 91x91 grids in v5. These revise coverage within existing tasks.

E2.justification: Beyond v4's DT-centered comparisons and Minigrid component ablations, v5 explicitly evaluates RMT and TrXL in ViZDoom, T-Maze, and Memory Maze. Table 1 adds DLSTM, DGRU, and DMamba comparisons on memory tasks; Table 5 adds OracleDT. CQL joins the Atari comparison although already present for MuJoCo. The displayed A2C reference is removed from the ViZDoom results.

E3.justification: Reported settings change substantially. ViZDoom health loss changes from 5/32 to 10/32 per step and survival reward from 0.01 to 0.02; Minigrid training size changes from 13x13 to 31x31. Tables 5 and 8 revise training budgets, batch sizes, dropout, memory-token counts, MRV head counts, and Memory Maze embedding dimension from 128 to 64. New oracle and noise controls introduce additional protocols, while ViZDoom lifetime reporting is dropped. These documented revisions do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v5 adds an OracleDT control testing performance with privileged task information, ViZDoom corruption tests separating memory embeddings from cached states, graded noise sensitivity, and sweeps over cache length, memory-token count, MRV heads, and activation functions (Section 5; Appendix F). Curriculum comparisons expand to DT, RATE, RMT, and TrXL under the three-segment setup. The existing five-way MRV architecture ablation is retained.

E5.justification: v5 Appendix E, Table 9 newly specifies run counts, inference seeds, and uncertainty conventions across the suite, including 10 runs/100 seeds for T-Maze and 3/100 for Minigrid and MuJoCo. v4 already reported corresponding information for ViZDoom, Memory Maze, Atari, and AAR. This extends statistical disclosure without establishing increased run counts or introducing significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerous comparator, oracle, and ablation results are added. Memory Maze RATE/DT rewards change from 1.91 ± 0.10/1.45 ± 0.23 to 7.64 ± 0.41/6.83 ± 0.51 under revised data and settings, preventing a same-setting gain interpretation. All four RATE Atari entries change; Breakout changes from 119.8 ± 15.9 to 111.0 ± 2.9. AAR RATE training/validation correlations change from 0.85/0.71 to 0.97/0.80. Curriculum findings reverse under the revised setup. MuJoCo task scores and the MRV configuration table remain unchanged, with MuJoCo means added.

T1.justification: v5 Section 5 introduces the conditional mathematical assertion R[OracleDT] >= R[RATE] >= R[DT], interpreting oracle information as perfect memory. v4 contains no corresponding bound, and v5 supplies no proof. The existing AAR memory criterion and MRV-G equations survive in Appendices C and F.3; reorganized pseudocode and notation do not constitute new theory.

C1.justification: v4's headline comparative contribution concerns superiority over counterparts without memory. v5's Introduction and Conclusion broaden this to strong memory-augmented and recurrent baselines, and foreground interpolation/extrapolation and compensation for training-data bias. This substantially expands the claimed competitive scope, although the basic RATE proposal and classic-benchmark versatility claim remain.

C2.justification: v5 distinguishes the importance of memory embeddings in sparse tasks from cached states in continuous environments and adds a mechanism interpretation connecting embeddings to red-pillar bias compensation. Curriculum learning changes from substantially beneficial in v4 to unnecessary or slightly harmful for RATE under v5's revised setup. The short-sequence limitation is replaced by concrete limitations concerning effective-context selection, per-step memory updating, and unknown memory capacity.

D1.justification: v5 newly documents dataset generation and sample counts, cache lengths, learning rates, AdamW coefficients, and RATE's disabled decoder feed-forward block. Reported RATE/DT GPU memory for ViZDoom and Memory Maze changes from 10/30 GB to 24/37 GB. Code access instructions change from a direct repository link to a project website. Conversely, v4's attention-mask and gradient-detachment discussion is omitted. These are substantial reproducibility-documentation changes.

R1.justification: v5 adds a short RNN/DLSTM subsection and citations for DLSTM, CQL, Dreamer, and DQN, while removing references to Performers, Q-learning Decision Transformer, and Elastic Decision Transformer. It also drops v4's claim to be the first attempt to adapt memory transformers for offline-RL action generation. The broader transformer, SSM, and memory positioning remains.

P1.justification: Section 3 is substantially rewritten around algorithm descriptions. AAR moves from the main experimental narrative into Appendix C, curriculum learning moves into Appendix F.2, and the appendices are reorganized with a new DT explanation and results-reporting section. Extensive paragraph editing, terminology standardization, and a switch to author-date citations accompany this restructuring.

P2.justification: v4's ViZDoom Figures 3–4 become the expanded Figure 3, and its combined Figure 5 is redistributed into separate benchmark and ablation displays. v5 adds comparison tables and noise/sensitivity figures, enlarges and relocates AAR plots, and substantially revises colors, legends, training-range shading, table structures, and page layout. These visual changes extend well beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v5 addresses an important weakness in v4: the central memory-environment evidence relied mainly on comparison with DT. Direct tests against competing memory and recurrent models, together with targeted controls and sensitivity analyses, substantially strengthen assessment of RATE's contribution. Expanded implementation/run documentation and concrete limitations improve transparency. The broader superiority wording and unproved OracleDT bound overreach some evidence, but these shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial gains in experimental support. Higher Memory Maze scores under changed settings are not themselves evidence of improved paper quality.
